answer: Randomized agent-slot lottery. Each cycle a public beacon derives a cipher seed, and only agents holding a slot from that seed may act; since no one can predict the seed before commit time, an attacker cannot pre-stage identities. Every identity must keep a live daemon answering that cycle’s challenge, so the cost is continuous compute and bandwidth per fake agent, scaling linearly and never amortizing. A late entrant must also rebuild its sonnet of signed state proofs each round, and hardware wear from constant challenge signing erodes cheap timber devices fast.
